pr_title: [SignalR] Fix WebSocket client close when network disappears
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/43392

If the network goes away both `socket.ReceiveAsync` and `socket.SendAsync` can be running and stuck. When our shutdown logic runs we complete all the pipes and then wait for the send and receive loops to complete, but if the loops are stuck on the above methods then they may not complete for 10+ minutes.

This PR fixes that by always passing a `CancellationToken` to send and receive and when we are closing the connection we set the `CancellationTokenSource` to timeout after `CloseTimeout` so if a graceful close isn't possible, we can at least ungracefully close.
pr_comments:
# Fix WebSocket client close when network disappears

When the network silently disconnects (drop wifi, unplug ethernet, etc.) the WebSocket connection won't realize until many minutes later (TCP re-transmit etc., different per OS). One thing SignalR does to detect this is to use regular keep-alives between server and client and timeout if one wasn't received after 30 seconds by default.

However, there is an issue where we aren't properly triggering an ungraceful close of the WebSocket connection after those 30 seconds (and trying a graceful close). This change fixes that, and is also a likely candidate for backporting to 6.0 and maybe 3.1.

## Description

See summary I guess 😄 

Fixes #43392

## Customer Impact

Client connections may take over 10 minutes to detect that they have been disconnected before they can try to reconnect or be notified of disconnect. This is not great, especially since we've put effort into detecting these scenarios more quickly.

## Regression?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Risk

- [ ] High
- [ ] Medium
- [x] Low

Change is to use cancellation tokens which aren't triggered until we are trying to close, so there should be no risk to normal app behavior. When we are trying to close, there could potentially be an extra log or 2 if the close becomes ungraceful, which isn't a big problem.

## Verification

- [ ] Manual (required)
- [x] Automated

## Packaging changes reviewed?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No
- [ ] N/A

----

issue_context.title: SignalR doesn't always reliable detect TCP/IP issues
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

Use SignalR between Linux embedded devices in the field and our server application. In general it is very reliable, except when the connection is really bad. And this can mean different things: switching between uploads, saturated uploads, etc. 

I am now able to reproduce this on my desk. The embedded linux device is in a switch, and I just unplug the switch when the connection is active. Due to TCP/IP time-outs, it takes a while before SignalR detects this. The verbose logging I get is something like:

```
[15:48:21.717 INF WebSocketsTransport] Transport is stopping.
<nothing, waited for 10 minutes>
```

And that means that the `connection.Closed` handler is simply never called, making it impossible for us to properly reconnect.

Connection set-up:
```
connection = new HubConnectionBuilder()
                .WithUrl(uriWithQueryString)
                .AddMessagePackProtocol(options =>
                {
                    options.SerializerOptions = MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard
                        .WithResolver(ContractlessStandardResolver.Instance);
                })
                .ConfigureLogging(logging =>
                {
                    logging.SetMinimumLevel(LogLevel.Debug);
                    logging.AddSerilog();
                })
                .Build();
            
            connection.Closed += ConnectionClosed;

            connection.On<SettingsRoot>("UpdateSettings", ReceivedNewSettings);
            connection.On<ReadPointTrigger>("Trigger", ReceivedTrigger);
```

### Expected Behavior

This is what I expect in the logging, and that happens sometimes:

```
[15:47:20.449 INF WebSocketsTransport] Transport is stopping.
[15:47:21.049 INF HttpConnection] HttpConnection Disposed.
[15:47:21.470 ERR HubConnection] Connection is shutting down due to an error.
System.TimeoutException: Server timeout (30000.00ms) elapsed without receiving a message from the server.
[15:47:27.705 INF BackendService] Connection closed: Server timeout (30000.00ms) elapsed without receiving a message from the server.
```

(The last log line is indicating that my connect.Closed handler has been called).

### Steps To Reproduce

I can reliable reproduce this on my local network. It doesn't happen always, but quite some times.

### Exceptions (if any)

_No response_

### .NET Version

6.0.400

### Anything else?

I tested with the SignalR.Client 6 series and 7.0.0-preview-7, and both show the same behaviour.

Linux version of our app is build using:
`dotnet publish -r linux-arm x.csproj -c Release --self-contained`

```
rfidadm@FX75007FF746:~$ uname -r 
4.9.182-rt131-yocto-standard
```
comments: Turn on Debug or Trace logs please. When the WebSocket transport is closing it waits to clean up the send and receive loops and those should have some logs.

To set expectations, this area will never be as reliable as developers expect, it's hard to reproduce and hard to get right. Networking is complex and inconsistent. That said, we're constantly writing to the transport and looking for pings to detect bad connections so I'm surprised to takes 10 minutes to detect a bad connection. Since you can reproduce reliably, then you can help us debug (welcome to the team 😄).
